jobs.occupation: Senior Product Manager
jobs.description:
This position is open to candidates located anywhere in Europe.

_At Basware, we deliver mission-critical cloud solutions that empower organizations to unlock their full potential. Our products are designed to bring clear and compelling value to our customers, and we’re looking for talented and forward-thinking professionals who can help us shape the future of our technology.

_Basware is seeking a Senior Product Manager to own our AI-native document capture solution. This role covers both the product itself, the vision, strategy, and roadmap, and the AI process behind it: the extraction models, the feedback loop, and the training pipeline that improve accuracy over time. The Senior Product Manager will work closely with engineering, architecture, UX, sales, and customer success throughout the product lifecycle.

_The position is open to candidates based in Europe, and applicants must have authorization to work within Europe.

_**Key Responsibilities

**

• Own product strategy and roadmap for AI-native document capture, with a clear view of where competitors are moving and where Basware needs to move faster.

• Own the AI process end to end: the multi-model extraction architecture with automatic failover, the feedback and training loop, and how field corrections become model improvements.

• Set the ground truth and accuracy measurement strategy so product accuracy is a measured fact, not a talking point.

• Apply Basware's Governed Autonomy framework to AI decisions in the product: define the limits and ensure every action stays explainable, auditable, and accountable.

• Engage directly with customers, prospects, and partners in sales cycles, field visits, and feedback sessions to shape the roadmap and reduce friction to adoption.

• Partner with sales, marketing, and partner teams to drive usage and adoption.

• Track the KPIs that measure this product's contribution to adoption and AI-driven revenue, and use them to inform the roadmap.

,

**Requirements

**

• Experience: 5+ years of product management experience, including 2+ years specifically shaping AI/ML-powered products or features, with a strong background in ILM or financial technology

• Domain Knowledge: Deep understanding of AP processes

• AI/ML Fluency: Real working knowledge of AI/ML technologies; comfortable making product trade-off calls on model behavior, confidence, and evaluation rather than relying on a vendor's claims

• AI Governance: Sound judgment on where AI should act autonomously and where it shouldn't, and experience designing controls that hold up to audit

• Customer-Centric Mindset: Ability to translate customer pain points into product solutions

• Leadership & Collaboration: Strong communication and stakeholder management skills to align cross-functional teams

• Analytical Thinking: Strong data analysis skills, including accuracy measurement and error attribution, to drive product decisions

**About Basware

**Basware is the global leader in Invoice Lifecycle Management, processing more than 250 million invoices a year across 190+ countries, backed by more than $10 trillion in cumulative invoice value and over 40 years of industry expertise. Basware was named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Accounts Payable Applications.

**Why join us?

**

• You'll own outcomes, not just a roadmap. What you decide ships, and you'll see the effect in weeks, not years.

• Every correction your team makes feeds a system running across 175+ countries. Few product roles let you touch this much of a company's core value chain.

• We measure you on results, not activity. If you want your name on the numbers, not just the backlog, you'll fit right in.

**Our offering

**We offer flexibility in how you work, giving you the freedom and support to deliver your best results. As a company, we are committed to your well-being and want to make sure you have an excellent work-life balance. We offer you an opportunity to build your career in an international environment and to develop and learn continuously.

What sets us apart is our unique company culture. At Basware, collaboration is at the core of everything we do. The 'We' spirit unites us and fosters a sense of inclusion, igniting a genuine passion for success and a shared celebration of achievements. Regardless of our backgrounds, we are all Baswareans.

This role is based in Europe, with flexibility to work from a Basware office or in a hybrid setup. Because of close day-to-day collaboration with our engineering and product teams, overlap with European working hours is required.

**Ready to make an impact?

**If you're excited by the challenge, **apply now and help shape the future of Basware.

**Please submit your resume and cover letter by clicking the ‘I’m interested’ link.

Our recruitment process will include pre-employment actions such as enhanced background screening and reference check.

**Basware. Now it all just happens.

**

jobs.occupation: Senior Jewelry Designer - Interim
jobs.description:
Are you a passionate jewellery designer with extensive experience creating iconic products and collections? Do you combine a strong creative vision with exceptional sketching skills and a deep understanding of craftsmanship, materials and the jewellery design process?

We are looking for an experienced Senior Designer to join our Modern Classics & Diamonds team on a 12-month fixed-term contract, bringing creative expertise and immediate impact to one of Pandora's key jewellery categories.

Create the next generation of Modern Classics & Diamonds

As our Senior Designer, Modern Classics & Diamonds, you will work closely with the Design Director and wider design team to develop creative projects from initial concept through design execution and prototype development.

Drawing on your creative vision, technical expertise and understanding of Pandora's brand DNA, you will help develop compelling, commercially relevant collections that combine timeless elegance with modern expression and inspire customers around the world.

Your Role

Design & Collection Development

• Partner with the team to create and develop new collections within the Modern Classics & Diamonds category.

• Translate creative briefs into innovative product concepts, designs and sketches aligned with Pandora's brand identity.

• Lead individual design projects from research and concept development through CAD and prototype stages.

• Propose original and future-thinking product ideas supporting the strategic direction of the category.

• Develop mood boards, concept presentations, creative sketches and technical drawings to support product development.

• Review CADs and provide clear and comprehensive creative feedback within agreed timelines.

• Brief products to Design Operations & Development (DoD) and collaborate closely to ensure successful prototype execution.

• Review early prototypes and contribute to formal prototype reviews and creative evaluations.

• Collaborate with Creative Sourcing to explore new materials, techniques and innovation opportunities.

• Partner with Creative Merchandising to align category and collection structures.

• Maintain accurate design documentation, inspiration references and project records throughout the design process.

• Support and mentor Junior Designers, providing creative and technical guidance.

• Ensure projects are developed and delivered according to agreed timelines and requirements.

Research & Innovation

• Conduct research based on briefs from Creative Leadership and translate insights into strong creative concepts.

• Participate in research activities and trips to identify emerging trends, products, techniques, materials and creative inspiration.

• Contribute ideas for new concepts, innovation opportunities and future category directions.

• Keep design presentations updated with relevant concepts, sketches and final designs throughout project development.

A Creative Visionary with a Passion for Jewellery

You combine exceptional creativity with strong technical expertise and an instinct for commercially relevant product design. You know how to take an idea from inspiration and early sketches through to a beautifully resolved piece of jewellery.

You understand how to balance innovation with the DNA of an established global brand and are comfortable moving between creative exploration and the technical realities of product development.

As this is a 12-month fixed-term opportunity, we are particularly looking for someone who can quickly become part of the team, confidently take ownership of projects and contribute from day one.

What We're Looking For

• Significant experience designing jewellery within a jewellery, luxury, fashion or accessories brand.

• A strong creative portfolio demonstrating concept development, mood boards, sketches and finished products.

• Proven experience taking design projects from concept through CAD and prototype development.

• Strong knowledge of jewellery design, craftsmanship, materials and manufacturing processes.

• Exceptional hand-sketching and visual communication skills.

• Experience working with CAD development and cross-functional product development teams.

• Ability to translate creative direction into distinctive and commercially relevant products.

• Strong communication and collaboration skills within an international environment.

• Experience mentoring or supporting junior designers is an advantage.

• Proficiency in relevant design tools, including Adobe Illustrator, Photoshop and InDesign.

Important

Please include a portfolio as part of your application, showcasing your design work, creative process, sketching and technical capabilities, and examples of collections or products you have helped take from concept to final execution.

Applications without a portfolio may not be considered.

Your New Team

As a key member of Pandora's Product Design team, you will join an international group of passionate and highly skilled designers dedicated to creating beautiful and innovative jewellery.

You will report to the Design Director and collaborate closely with colleagues across Creative Direction, Design Operations & Development, Creative Merchandising, Creative Sourcing and Product Development.

Additional Information

This is a 12-month fixed-term contract based at Pandora's Global Office in Copenhagen, Denmark.

Did We Get Your Attention?

If you see yourself in this opportunity and would like to contribute to Pandora's future, we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

Please submit your CV and portfolio through our online application system. Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply at your earliest convenience.

Icing on the Cake

You will be working from our beautiful Global Office in Copenhagen V, established in 2016 and designed to unite and inspire our teams. Alongside our inspiring work environment, we are proud to hold LEED Gold Certification for Energy and Environmental Design, reflecting our commitment to sustainability and responsible use of resources.

The result is a professional and dynamic workspace that is unique, comfortable and inspirational, delivering a true Pandora experience to everyone who works here and visits our offices.

About Pandora

Pandora is the world's largest jewellery brand, specialising in the design, crafting and marketing of accessible luxury jewellery made from high-quality materials. Each piece is created to inspire self-expression, allowing people to share their stories and passions through meaningful jewellery. Pandora jewellery is sold in more than 100 countries through 7,000 points of sale, including more than 2,800 concept stores.

Headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark, Pandora employs around 39,000 people worldwide and crafts its jewellery with 100% recycled silver and gold. Pandora is committed to leadership in sustainability and has set out to halve greenhouse gas emissions across its value chain by 2030. Pandora is listed on the Nasdaq Copenhagen stock exchange and generated revenue of DKK 32.5 billion (EUR 4.4 billion) in 2025.

jobs.occupation: Staff scientist in the Human Organoid facility at the Novo Nordisk Foundation Center for Vaccines and Immunity
jobs.description:
The Novo Nordisk Foundation Center for Vaccines and Immunity (NIVI Research) seeks a staff scientist to join the Human Immune Organoids facility for a position of 3 years. The position will be available 1 January 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  NIVI Research is embedded in the Department of Immunology and Microbiology, Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen.

  Background
 The Novo Nordisk Foundation Initiative for Vaccines and Immunity (NIVI), launched in December 2023, has a unique mission to harness airway immunity through innovative vaccine research and development to prevent airborne epidemics. NIVI has two parts:

   	
• NIVI Research (NIVI-R): A state-of-the-art research center anchored to the University of Copenhagen, Department of Immunology and Microbiology (www.isim.ku.dk). 	
• NIVI Development (NIVI-D): A company that focuses on translational sciences and advancing vaccine development.   NIVI-R conducts scientific research, while NIVI-D works to quickly turn that research into new vaccine candidates. NIVI-D accelerates clinical trials (phases 1 and 2) and ensures a smooth transition to partners for later stages of development.

  By connecting science, innovation, clinical trials, regulatory processes, and product development, NIVI aims to streamline the journey from research to real-world vaccines.

  Who are we?
 The Human Organoid facility is a newly established research team within NIVI-R. It conducts independent research projects and runs a Human Organoid facility as a core resource for the research center. We primarily work with upper respiratory and immune organoids, which closely replicate human immune responses to pathogens and vaccines (Wagar, L. et al. Nature Medicine, 2021; Chen, X. & Ghanizada, M. et al. Nature Immunology, 2025). The team's research focus aligns with NIVI-R's overall goal of enhancing our understanding of human immune response and airway immunity. In addition, we will serve as a human organoid facility that collaborates closely with other groups at NIVI-R while continuing to develop organoid systems. The Human Organoid facility has approximately 5 members and is led by Mustafa Ghanizada, MD.

  Homepage:

  If you want to learn more, please visit: www.isim.ku.dk and https://nivi.ku.dk/

  Work assignments:
 The work assignments in the facility are:

   	
• Develop, establish, and maintain iPSC-based human cell and organoid models. 	
• To independently perform predefined research projects using iPSC-derived cell types, organoid models, and other human cell-based systems to address research questions related to human immunity, infection, and airway biology. 	
• To develop, optimize existing protocols, and experiment with new organoid models. 	
• To train people in organoid culture work and basic assays. 	
• To plan and perform experiments in collaboration with the other NIVI-R groups. 	
• To manage the organoid facility (e.g., overview of human sampling cohort, tissue processing, and experiment planning).   Much of the daily work is done independently. The successful candidate will be expected to plan and prioritize activities, coordinate with the facility team and collaborating research groups, troubleshoot unexpected challenges, and implement new experimental workflows.

  We are looking for a staff scientist with the following competencies and experience:

   	
• A person with strong knowledge of cell biology, or a closely related field, with an interest in applying human model systems to understand airway immune responses and respiratory infections. 	
• A person with at least 3 years of documented laboratory experience in advanced human cell culture, preferably involving iPSCs, human primary cells, or tissue-derived models. 	
• Hands-on experience with iPSC culture and/or iPSC-derived cell models, including experience with maintaining, expanding, differentiating, and characterizing iPSCs and/or iPSC-derived cells. 	
• Experience with organoid culture and/or developing 3D human models would be highly beneficial but not required. 	
• Experience with cellular and immunological assays, including immunostaining/imaging, cryo-sectioning, flow cytometry, ELISA, and similar methods. 	
• Demonstrated ability to independently design, plan, execute, troubleshoot, and interpret experiments. 	
• Experience in developing, optimizing, and establishing new experimental protocols, with a systematic approach to troubleshooting and improving reproducibility. 	
• Experience working with high-dimensional data and the ability to analyze, interpret, and communicate complex experimental datasets. 	
• An interest in human organoid models and human immunology. 	
• Strong interpersonal skills and an independent, collaborative mindset to support the mission. 	
• Experience in training and supervising students, lab technicians, or junior researchers, as well as in laboratory or facility management. 	
• You have a high degree of drive and pro-activeness with the ability to respond effectively to new tasks and changing priorities in a dynamic, project-driven research environment. 	
• You are a team player, goal-oriented, and have an innovative mindset, which allows you to put forth new ideas and make them practical. 	
• Ability to organize, plan, and execute administrative and organizational tasks independently, including experimental planning, scheduling, documentation, resource management, and prioritization of competing activities.   Qualifications:
 Education should be at Master of Science level or equivalent, preferably with a PhD in stem cell biology, cell biology, immunology, or a related field. You must have documented experience in advanced cell culture techniques. Your approach to the position should integrate independent research and the facility's services to foster collaboration with other NIVI-R research groups and their experiments.

  We offer:

   	
• Unique opportunities to become part of a solid new research program. 	
• International and stimulating workplace in constant development, working with the newest human organoid models under strong international leading collaborations. 	
• A versatile and exciting job with many challenges and a big influence on how the job is organized. 	
• A job that combines both part-time research and part-time facility management. 	
• A job with opportunities for participation in meetings/courses where relevant. 	
• A job where we constantly develop the facility with new protocols (e.g., optimize current organoid models and develop new). 	
• A job that offers flexibility. 	
• A job in a coherent group with an informal and relaxed work environment. 	
• Great infrastructure facilities located in central Copenhagen, Denmark.   Salary and terms of employment: 
 The employment as an academic research officer/staff scientist is a full-time position (37 hours per week) for 3 years starting 1 January 2027. Employment will be under The Circular on the Collective Agreement concerning Academics in the state sector concluded between the Danish Ministry of Finance and Akademikerne (the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations). There will be an opportunity to negotiate supplements based on qualifications. You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish). The applicable pension contribution will be in accordance with the relevant collective agreement.

  Application:
 Your application should be in English and include:

   	
• Letter of motivation addressing the requirements (max. one page) 	
• Curriculum Vitae (including 2 references) 	
• Publications list 	
• A certified/signed copy of the certificate(s) of education   Please submit your application by clicking on “Apply Now” below. 
 We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the above-mentioned requirements.

  Application deadline: 25 October 2026

  The University wishes to reflect the diversity of the surrounding society and encourages all qualified candidates, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. 

  Questions:
 For further information regarding the position, please contact Mustafa Ghanizada, MD, by email at m.ghanizada@sund.ku.dk

  The University of Copenhagen has established a new shared administrative organizational structure, which is currently being implemented. This entails ongoing changes and the development of, among other things, workflows and interfaces for collaboration.

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in AI-Driven Optimization of Optical Links based on Nano-Lasers - DTU Electro
jobs.description:
DTU Electro invites applications for a PhD position in AI-driven optimization of optical links based on nano-lasers, within the Villum Investigator program "Power-Efficient Fiber-Optic Communication" (POPCOM) and DNRF Center for NanoPhotonics (NANOPHOTON). The position focuses on developing signaling optimization frameworks to maximize spectral and power efficiency. 

As data-center traffic continues to grow, the energy consumption of optical links has become a critical bottleneck, with power efficiency (measured in J/bit) increasingly rivaling spectral efficiency as a key performance metric. This project will investigate how AI-driven techniques can jointly optimize nano-laser-based transmitters and their waveforms to reduce energy consumption while sustaining high data rates, contributing to more sustainable next-generation optical communication infrastructure. 

Responsibilities and qualifications
We seek a motivated, curious, and outgoing PhD candidate with a solid background in fiber optics, laser-physics, communication engineering, machine learning, and AI-based agentic frameworks. Experience applying machine learning or AI-based optimization frameworks to communication systems and laser modelling, as well as experimental work, is a plus.

The project goal is to develop an AI-driven optimization framework and apply it to realize robust transmitter and receiver architectures that enable power-efficient signaling at the maximum allowable spectral efficiency. The project will cover both algorithm development and experimental implementation.

We offer an opportunity to develop expertise in various domains, including but not limited to:

• Reinforcement learning for the design of optical links
• Development of nano-laser physical system models and data-driven models
• Realization of experimental procedures for testing the developed frameworks
• Building fiber-optic transmission systems
• Investigating transmission performance in practical test-beds
As a PhD candidate at DTU, you will take part in an educational program of 30 ECTS tailored to your needs, covering technical subjects as well as the "soft skills" needed for a successful career in industry or academia.

Your tasks will include research and development of AI-driven methods for mitigating impairments associated with short-range optical links, using energy-efficient signal processing solutions. The overall goal will be to maximize the information rate given the energy-consumption constraint. Specifically, you will focus on the following areas:

• Gradient-based learning for symbol and pulse shaping
• Model-free reinforcement learning strategies for signal pre-distortion
• Physics-informed neural networks
• Maintenance of the GitHub repository for the developed code
• Organizing and managing joint experiments with collaboration groups
You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures.

The period of employment is 3 years.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information 
Further information may be obtained from Professor Darko Zibar, dazi@dtu.dk and Professor Jesper Mørk jesm@dtu.dk.

You can read more about DTU Electro at https://electro.dtu.dk/. 

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later 1 November, 2026 (23:59 Danish time). Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it. 

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU Electro  
DTU Electro employs more than 300 skilled researchers with competencies in electrical and photonics engineering. As a department, we strive towards creating sustainable energy and a greener internet, as well as strengthening cyber security and health technology. Working with industry and public organizations is one of our top priorities to find and implement new solutions to our society. We aim to offer education, research, and innovation of the highest standard, and our focus on application-oriented research enables us to work across many engineering disciplines and research areas, such as IT and the medical and health sciences. We have a close collaboration with researchers from all over the world, just as we collaborate with industry and public authorities about the dissemination of solutions based on electrical and photonics engineering as their key enabling technologies. 

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

jobs.occupation: Operation Director for SCIENCE Makerspace
jobs.description:
Do you want to create something new? Do you want to fundamentally change how we organize teaching and learning at the SCIENCE departments? Do you want to be part of a unique opportunity in the largest university in Denmark? Then you might be our new SCIENCE Makerspace Operation Director.

  We invite applications for a 5-year position as Operation Director for the SCIENCE Makerspace at the Faculty of Science, University of Copenhagen. The Faculty of Science is committed to sustainably continuing the Makerspace activities at the end of the 5-year period, providing the possibility for extending the position long-term.

   

  About the SCIENCE Makerspace

  We are establishing a top-tier Makerspace at the Faculty of Science, University of Copenhagen, spearheaded by the Department of Computer Science (DIKU), Niels Bohr Institute (NBI), and the Department of Science Education (IND). The SCIENCE Makerspace vision is built upon a foundation of Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Belonging (DEIB) and aims to create an inclusive learning environment that bridges disciplines, supports different ways of learning, and attracts students with diverse backgrounds and interests. Everyone is welcome, and no prior knowledge of makerspaces, machines, or materials is required.

  The SCIENCE Makerspace will be established as a 600 sqm facility centrally located at Nørre Campus, with a budget of 42 million DKK over 5 years supported by the Novo Nordisk Foundation. The Makerspace is expected to host 1-3 university courses per academic quarter, independent projects for BSc/MSc/PhD students, and be a venue for extracurricular workshops and 'blue sky' ideas from faculty and students. The Makerspace will also facilitate the integration between traditional and non-traditional forms of knowledge production within an Expert-in-residence program.

  The Faculty of Science at the University of Copenhagen is one of Scandinavia's largest science faculties, with over 4,000 staff, ~9,000 students, and an annual turnover exceeding DKK 3 billion, located in the heart of Copenhagen. SCIENCE hosts 12 departments spanning a breadth of disciplines from molecular biology and chemistry to mathematics, computer science, and geoscience, united by a commitment to curiosity-driven, high-impact research. 

   

  Description of the position

  We offer a unique opportunity for you to become the Operation Director of the ‘yet-to-be-build' 600 sqm SCIENCE Makerspace centrally placed at the Northen Campus in Copenhagen. The SCIENCE Makerspace vision is to design, build and run an inclusive and innovative learning space that bridges disciplines, allows for multi-modal learning activities, and attracts a diversified and balanced cohort of students from different educational programs (BSc, MSc, PhD) across the 12 Departments.

  The Operations Director will direct the SCIENCE Makerspace and be the manager for the Makerspace team. The Operation Director is responsible for ensuring that principles for DEIB are mainstreamed in all decisions in the Makerspace. 

  You will be part of the core decision-making on how to organize, establish, and run the ‘one-of-a-kind' Makerspace. You will collaborate with committed faculty from DIKU, NBI, and IND in the establishing phases, and with the Deanery for Education for long-term engagement across the departments in making the Makerspace vision a reality.

  You will be part of hiring the team who will run the makerspace together with you including Technical Lab Manager, Lab Technician, and a group of student mentors.

  This is a unique opportunity to be part of creating something new, in the largest university in Denmark, which fundamentally will change how we organize teaching and learning at the SCIENCE departments.

   

  You will need four core competences to succeed in the position:

   	
• You will need skills and expertise which allow you to strategize and develop ideas which will foster success for the SCIENCE Makerspace vision. This includes the work of identifying and understanding upcoming challenges for e.g. DEIB [DK3] (organizationally, socially, technically, and spatially) and finding solutions, while pro-actively execute required actions. Further, the Operation director must be able to function within an ‘entrepreneurial atmosphere’ where everything is not settled yet. 	
• You will need leadership and management competences which will allow you to lead a mixed Makerspace team of both highly skilled lab manager and lab technicians whose work requires levels of trust and autonomy, as well as student mentors who need clear instructions and guidance. 	
• You will need to navigate and understand the organizational and social structures of academia and university life, this includes considering the intrinsic motivation of researchers/teachers and PhD students, and how they might differ for MSc/BSc students. Such competence can arrive from your own experience during your education and does not require that you have worked in a university setting previously. 	
• You need interest in ‘making’ and Makerspaces. Furthermore, it is important that you consider consulting relevant experts about their views and perspectives, which will allow you to take qualitatively and well-founded decisions about our joint Makerspace.   You will not be a one-person army, instead you will have three main groups with different types of competences and experiences you can draw on in the position, including the Makerspace team, an experienced team of administrative management colleagues, and the Faculty of SCIENCE teaching committee.

  To read more about the vision, plans, and background for the SCIENCE Makerspace, please visit ucphmakerspace.dk

   

  Qualifications

  You are pro-active, find solutions where others see barriers, and are excited about being a core part of establishing, building, and running the brand-new SCIENCE Makerspace at University of Copenhagen, Denmark. 

  You have a relevant higher education or experience from similar positions. 

  You care for students and want to make it possible for all students at SCIENCE to experience learning activities where ‘making’ plays a role, e.g. as part of courses, project work, tech workshops, and extracurricular activities. 

  You are committed to the agenda of Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Belonging (DEIB), know about Universal Design, and strongly believe that all activities and decisions in the pioneer SCIENCE Makerspace must take into account the multiple, intersecting dimensions of groups including, but not limited to genders, internationality, neurodiversity, socioeconomic backgrounds, and physical feasibility.

  Our ideal candidate can be described as:

   	
• Have management experience - potentially from a university or a politically governed organization. 	
• Demonstrates a high degree of trust under responsibility towards our employees, who are self-driven and accountable. As a manager, you help set the overall direction, contribute to daily well-being and cohesion, and support the development of individual employees and the team, while maintaining an overview of strategic initiatives in collaboration with your staff. 	
• Has an understanding of others’ work situations, you are able to develop strong collaborative relationships across employees with different educational and professional backgrounds. 	
• You have personal or professional making experience, pedagogical expertise and DEIB expertise 	
• You are structured, service-minded, approachable, and able to build commitment to strategic decisions. 	
• You thrive in a diverse environment with a wide variety of tasks. 	
• You have collaboration skills and the ability to build networks across professional groups, including across the organization 	
• You have strong communication skills in English (oral and written) and is ready to learn Danish.    

  Living in Copenhagen

  The university is situated in Copenhagen, which is consistently rated among the world's top 10 most livable cities. Located in Denmark, ranked in the top three happiest countries globally, Copenhagen boasts a vibrant culture, rich in music, theater, and community organizations. Life for families is made easier via a publicly supported daycare and healthcare system, dual-career opportunities, maternity/parental leave, and six weeks of annual vacation. International candidates may find information on living and working in Denmark. Useful information is also available at the university’s International Staff Mobility (ISM) office, which offers a variety of services to international researchers coming to and working at the University of Copenhagen.

   

  Terms of employment

  The Operation Director reports to the Head of Administration, Department of Computer Science, Camilla Lillholm. You will be employed as a senior consultant with managerial responsibility in accordance with the collective agreement for academics in the state sector. There is an opportunity to negotiate additional allowances based on qualifications.

  Note that Denmark protects the economic, social, and physical well-being of its workers, which includes robust health care, childcare, elder care, and other generous benefits. Thus, direct salary comparisons across nations are typically not meaningful.

   

  Further information

  For dedicated information on the new Makerspace, go here: ucphmakerspace.dk

  You are welcome to contact Head of Administration, Department of Computer Science, Camilla Lillholm (camillaj@di.ku.dk), or the Academic Director Professor Pernille Bjørn (pernille.bjorn@di.ku.dk) if you have any inquiries about the position.

   

  Filing of application

  As part of the application for the position, please write and submit a 1-page appendix labeled "Core Competences - NAME” in English, where you answer the below questions (one paragraph for each question), considering the description of the position as well as the SCIENCE Makerspace vision, which you can read more about at ucphmakerspace.dk.
 You are not allowed to use AI when writing the appendix. The questions are:

   	
• What is your approach for leadership and management of the SCIENCE Makerspace 	
• What makes you excited about the SCIENCE Makerspace?  	
• What do you expect will be the most challenging part of making the SCIENCE Makerspace vision a reality?   Please submit your application, including appendix, CV and relevant documentation, electronically via the Job Portal (click the link “APPLY FOR THE POSITION” at the bottom of the advertisement), so that it reaches us no later than 14 November 2026. We expect to hold interviews on 27 November 2026 and 4 December 2026.

  The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the diversity of society and encourages all qualified candidates to apply regardless of age, disability, gender, nationality, race, religion, or sexual orientation. Appointments will be based solely on qualifications.

jobs.occupation: Full-Stack Software Engineer (Mid/Senior)
jobs.description:
Highlights:

• Full-Stack Python/TS engineer needed for a B2B SaaS startup in Copenhagen (with plenty of traction!)

• We have a lean, get-stuff-done team. No annoying extra management layers or unnecessary bureaucratic rituals. And we are "AI-forward" in our own development practices.

• You will own features end to end, from the data model through to the screen, on a platform that manufacturers rely on to keep production lines running.

• You will work in a small engineering team, directly with the person who decides what we build, and the problems you spend your time on are hard because the domain is hard, not because the organization is.

• We're building legitimately useful tools for the industries and companies that make the world go around.... manufacturers. Both AI-tools and just "plain-old-good-software" tools.

About Supplios

Manufacturers live or die by their supply base. Sourcing the wrong supplier, onboarding one slowly, failing to qualify one properly or losing track of a non-conformance can stop a production line and cost millions. Yet most manufacturers still run these relationships across email chains, spreadsheets and shared drives.

Supplios is a supplier collaboration platform for manufacturers in automotive and industrial sectors. We cover the full supplier relationship: sourcing, onboarding, qualification, day-to-day collaboration, compliance and supplier quality, all in a modern cloud based platform that is easy for manufacturers to implement and operate. It is built specifically for the way automotive and industrial manufacturers actually work.

We are headquartered in central Copenhagen and already serve customers globally in our vertical, including some of the most demanding names in automotive. We have grown to this point almost entirely on product strength, domain credibility and word of mouth.

The platform now covers more ground than the team that built it. We are hiring engineers to keep that pace sustainable, and to go deeper on the parts of the product our customers are pushing hardest.

The role

You will join a small engineering team and work across the whole stack: Python on the backend, TypeScript on the frontend and in the AI layers. There is no split between people who design and people who implement. You will take a problem from a customer conversation or a product decision through to something running in production for real manufacturers.

You will work directly with our co-founder and CEO, who is a hands-on product builder himself. That means short conversations instead of tickets thrown over a wall, and it means your questions about why something should work a certain way get answered by the person who decided it.

The domain is genuinely complicated, and that is the interesting part. Supplier relationships in automotive involve deep hierarchies, long-running approval processes, strict audit requirements and a lot of state that has to be exactly right. Modeling that well is most of the job.

Title and level flex with experience. We are open to strong mid-level engineers and to senior engineers who want more scope than their current company gives them.

We work together from our office in central Copenhagen. This is primarily an in-office role: at this stage, and on a codebase with this much implicit context, working through problems with the rest of the team in person is much faster than doing it in writing. Sensible flexibility when you need it is a given; full-time remote is not what we are offering.

Our current stack:

• Backend: Python / Django

• Frontend: Vue (but no specific Vue experience is needed)

• Infrastructure: AWS (mostly)

• Agents: Cloudflare (TypeScript) + Claude & OpenAI platform

What you will do

• Build features end to end, from data model and backend logic through to the TypeScript frontend our customers actually click on.

• Build end-to-end / front-to-back AI features (in-app AI assistants, background worker agents, email-routing agents, customer-configurable agent framework components)

• Design and evolve the relational data model that sits under supplier relationships, approvals and quality records.

• Take vaguely defined customer problems and turn them into something specific enough to build, then build it.

• Work on integrations between Supplios and customer systems (ERP and adjacent tooling), where failures have visible consequences for a production line.

• Improve the parts of the codebase that need it, rather than routing around them.

• Review other people's code and have yours reviewed; we keep the loop tight and unbureaucratic.

• Help keep the platform healthy in production across our regions: errors, performance and the boring things that keep customers trusting us.

• Take part in product decisions. Engineers here are expected to have opinions about what we build, not just how.

What we are looking for

Essential

• Professional experience with Python. This is not negotiable; the backend is Python and you need to be effective in it.

• Solid TypeScript experience and genuine comfort working on the frontend.

• Experience building and running SaaS products, including the part after launch where real users depend on them.

• AI-forward development techniques. (This does not mean you no longer write code.)

• A track record of owning work end to end without waiting to be told what to do next.

• The temperament for a small, senior company: high ownership, low ceremony.

• You want to work primarily from an office in central Copenhagen, with a small team.

Nice to have

Genuinely a plus, not a requirement. Nobody has all of these.

• Experience with B2B enterprise SaaS, especially where customers are large and demanding and implementations are not self-serve. This is a significant plus.

• Experience with complex relational data modeling, and with large, long-lived codebases that you did not write yourself. A big plus.

• Experience building AI-based products, using the latest frameworks/harnesses and infrastructure components (including RAG) is a significant plus.

• Familiarity with any of: domain-driven design, the actor model, finite state machines, CQRS, event-driven architecture. We use these ideas where they earn their place, and it helps if the vocabulary is already yours.

• Startup experience, particularly early stage. A significant plus.

• Knowledge of manufacturing, automotive or supply chain. Useful, but we can teach you the domain; we cannot teach you the craft, so do not rule yourself out on this.

Language

English is the only important language for this position; we work in English, and so do our customers. Danish language skills are not required.

Why this role is worth your time

• The scope is unusually large for the stage. You are one of a small number of engineers on a platform that serves demanding customers globally. What you build ships, and it ships soon.

• No layers between you and the decisions. You work directly with the co-founder and CEO, who runs product. There is no committee to navigate and nobody to translate your work for you.

• Hard problems that are not artificially hard. The complexity comes from the domain (hierarchies, state, audit trails, integrations that must not fail), not from organisational overhead.

• Real customers already, and real gaps. The product has paying customers in automotive and clear places where it needs to get better. Both halves of that are true, and both are why this is a good job.

How to apply

Send your CV and a short note on why this role interests you to team@supplios.com. Work examples will help.

Apply by email

Send an email to team@supplios.com

Please include your CV / resume, and a brief note about why you're interested in the position.

Thanks!

jobs.occupation: Postdoc position in the intellectual history of corporate politics
jobs.description:
Copenhagen Business School invites applications for a postdoc position in the field of the intellectual history of corporate politics at the Department of Business Humanities and Law. The expected starting date is 1 May, 2027 or as agreed upon by consultation. The postdoc position is a non-tenured full-time position of 2 years, with the possibility of 1 additional year of teaching obligations.

The research will be conducted as part of the Independent Research Fund Denmark Sapere Aude Grant project Visions of corporate politics: Intellectual histories of the state-firm analogy. The project team will consist of the PI, one postdoc and one PhD.
Read more about the project here: https://dff.dk/en/our-funded-projects/meet-the-researchers/research-leaders/eksterne-personer-en/research-leaders-2025/mathias-hein-jessen/

The central objective of the research project is to analyze contemporary contestations over the state-firm boundary as well as mobilizations of analogies between state and firm in projecting political and economic visions. The project analyzes the constitution of the state-firm distinction as well as what it terms contemporary ‘visions of corporate politics’ represented by ideologically distinct answers to the crisis of liberal democracy which both contest the state-firm boundary and mobilize the state-firm analogy to legitimize their vision: On the one hand attempts to democratize or politicize the firm and on the other hand attempts to build political communities on principles of corporate governance. The postdoc project will focus on one of the two contemporary visions of corporate politics.

Examples of potential research topics: the democratization of the firm; democratic or economic planning; employee ownership; platform cooperativism or socialism; network states; gov-corps; start-up governments; freedom cities.

The research conducted will be team-based and oriented towards delivering on the project objectives. Taking the project framework into consideration, applicants are required to outline their reflections on how to approach the study.

The position is mainly in-place. The candidate should be able to be regularly present and attend meetings in Copenhagen.

For more information about the position, please contact PI of the project Associate Professor Mathias Hein Jessen (mhj.bhl@cbs.dk). 

Research environment
The Department of Business Humanities and Law is dedicated to an integrated approach to the contemporary challenges facing business and society drawing on the humanities, interdisciplinary social sciences, and law. The core research areas of the Department of Business Humanities and Law are organized into different research Units: Governance, Culture and Learning; Entrepreneurship, Ethics and Leadership; and CBS Law. Faculty within these groups have research backgrounds in areas of political science, sociology, philosophy, history, anthropology, law, theology, aesthetics, design and innovation, tourism and leisure management, cultural economics, leadership and strategy, pedagogic study, and other areas. What unites faculty in our department is an overriding concern for the organization of the human within its multiple environments: work, nature, economy, civil association, the state, and corporation. 

Teaching responsibilities of the Department comprise undergraduate and graduate teaching as well as teaching in post-experience and doctoral education. Some programs are taught in Danish, some in English.

Within the Department of Business Humanities and Law, the position will be located in the Governance, Culture and Learning Unit, an interdisciplinary research environment connecting governance studies at all levels of global society. 

Qualifications
The ideal candidate will have completed a PhD in intellectual history, history, political sociology, political theory or political philosophy. The candidate will be committed to an academic career, have the capabilities to conduct internationally recognized research and be able to communicate findings clearly. 

The assessment of the candidate will be based primarily on the following qualifications:

• Excellent academic track record
• Research within the history of political, economic or legal thought, political theory, or political philosophy.
• The ability and desire to work autonomously and as part of a team
• Excellent organizational and communication skills (both oral and written); proficiency in English is required
• Ability to engage with others in a way that reflects a collective commitment to diversity, equality, and inclusion. 
The application (see link below) must include a 3-5-page project description. The project description must include:

• a presentation of an original research question
• a description of the initial theoretical framework and method
• a presentation of the proposed material
• a work plan for the project
Application procedure
All applications must be sent via the electronic recruitment system, using the link below. The application must include:

A complete, numbered list of publications and work in progress (indicating titles, co-authors, page numbers and year) with an * marking of the academic productions to be considered during the review.

The application must include:

• Cover letter outlining motivation, fit, and qualifications
• A project description
• Transcripts (Master's and PhD) and a full CV
• A complete, numbered list of publications (indicating titles, co-authors, page numbers and year) with an * marking of the academic productions to be considered during the review. A maximum of 5 publications for review is allowed. Applicants are requested to prioritise their publications in relation to the field of this job advertisement.
• Copies of the publications marked with an *. Only publications written in English (or another specified principal language, according to research tradition) or one of the Scandinavian languages will be taken into consideration)
• Any relevant information indicating experience in research management, industry co-operation, and international cooperation.
• Documentation of pedagogical qualifications or related material.
Closing date: 15 December 2026

Recruitment procedure
The Recruitment Committee will shortlist a minimum of two applicants. If possible, five or more applicants will be shortlisted. The shortlisted applicants will be assessed by the Assessment Committee. All applicants will be notified of their status in the recruitment process shortly after the application deadline. The applicants selected for assessment will be notified about the composition of the Assessment Committee and later in the process about the result of the assessment. An appointment committee will invite a selection of qualified candidates to an interview. Once the recruitment process is completed each applicant will be notified of the outcome of their application.

Appointment
Appointment and salary will be in accordance with the Ministry of Finance’s agreement with the Central Academic Organization. Information about CBS as a workplace is available at www.cbs.dk/en/about-cbs/jobs-cbs. 

For further information, please contact: PI of the project Associate Professor Mathias Hein Jessen, email: mhj.bhl@cbs.dk, or Head of Department Pia Bramming, e-mail pib.bhl@cbs.dk. Information about the department may be found at www.cbs.dk/bhl. Information about Copenhagen Business School is available at https://www.cbs.dk/en.

Copenhagen Business School must receive all application material, including all appendices (see items above), by the application deadline.

Copenhagen Business School invites all qualified candidates to apply for the position. An appointment committee will review the applications and invite a selection of qualified candidates to an interview.

One of CBS’ strategic goals is the promotion of diversity, which is why every effort has been made to ensure a recruitment process that reduces potential bias. Applicants are therefore encouraged not to include a photo or unnecessary personal information in their application.

Details about Copenhagen Business School and the department are available at www.cbs.dk.
